wines.name: Continental Platter Prosecco
wines.winemaking: Tank method (Charmat) on organically and biodynamically farmed Glera. Fresh fruit character preserved, no lees ageing.
wines.producer: Continental Platter, King Valley, Victoria. A project led by acclaimed Victorian winemaker Patrick Sullivan.
wines.convNote: Continental Platter is a project from Patrick Sullivan, one of Victoria's most respected natural winemakers -- known for serious, minimal-intervention wines from the Gippsland and beyond. This Prosecco is his accessible, fun side project: organic and biodynamic Glera from the King Valley, made simply to be smashable. Lemon zest, lime sherbet, green apple, a touch of honey, bright acidity. Easy opener for anyone, with real winemaking pedigree behind it.

wines.name: Ca del Bosco Brut
wines.winemaking: Traditional method: bottle fermented, 25+ months on lees. Comparable to Champagne.
wines.convNote: This is serious Italian fizz. Think toasted hazelnut, baked apple, a whisper of honey, and that long chalky finish that makes you want another sip. Franciacorta is Italy's answer to Champagne -- same method, same grapes, different sun. Ca' del Bosco has been making this since 1968 and it shows.

wines.name: Pippa Pet Nat
wines.winemaking: Pet Nat: bottled mid-fermentation, finishes naturally. Unfiltered -- expect slight haze.
wines.convNote: The wild child of the sparkling section. Petillant naturel is the oldest sparkling method -- bottled before it finishes fermenting so it's alive, a little hazy, a little unpredictable. Wild strawberry, white nectarine, lemon sherbet. Great for adventurous guests or anyone who wants something with a story.

wines.name: Cantine Riccardi Reale Divago
wines.winemaking: Sparkling red: refermented in bottle. Dry, tannic -- unusual for a fizz.
wines.convNote: A sparkling red -- yes, really. Cesanese is Rome's local red grape and it almost never gets made fizzy. Dark cherry, violet, a little earthy, with real tannin grip. Order this for the table that wants to try something they've never had before.

wines.name: Ferrari Perle
wines.winemaking: Traditional method. 5+ years on lees before release. Single vineyard, high alpine.
wines.convNote: The most serious bottle in the sparkling section. Ferrari (no relation to the car) has been making traditional-method wine in Trentino since 1902. This is aged for five years before release -- toasted brioche, white truffle, baked apple, extraordinary length. For guests celebrating something special.

wines.name: Cave Mont Blanc
wines.winemaking: Stainless steel. No oak, no malo. Pure alpine freshness.
wines.producer: Valle d'Aosta -- Italy's smallest wine region
wines.convNote: From some of the highest vineyards in Europe -- up to 1,200 metres in the Italian Alps between France and Switzerland. Prie Blanc is grown almost nowhere else. The result is impossibly fresh: green apple, alpine herbs, flint, chalk. Feels like cold mountain air in a glass.

wines.name: Visintini
wines.winemaking: Cool stainless steel. High natural acidity needs minimal intervention.
wines.convNote: Ribolla Gialla has been growing in the Collio hills near Slovenia since the 13th century. This is the textbook expression -- lemon verbena, green pear, a saline mineral edge from the ancient ponca soils. Bright, clean, and very food-friendly.

wines.name: Muri-Gries
wines.winemaking: Stainless steel. Early harvest for acid tension. No malolactic fermentation.
wines.producer: Benedictine abbey in Bolzano's Gries district; monastic winegrowing here goes back centuries, with Benedictine monks from Muri in Switzerland tending the vines since 1845.
wines.convNote: A monastery in Bolzano's Gries district with centuries of winegrowing tradition -- Benedictine monks from Switzerland took it over in 1845. Their Silvaner is nothing like the German version: more precise, more mineral, with white grapefruit, green herbs, and a clean chalky finish. Alto Adige is bilingual and the wines reflect that duality.

wines.name: Terre Stregate Trama
wines.winemaking: Stainless steel. Brief lees contact adds body.
wines.convNote: Falanghina may descend from the wines drunk in ancient Rome. This version comes from volcanic Campania -- white peach, lemon blossom, a fennel-like freshness, and that volcanic mineral note underneath everything. Good value, easy to recommend across the board.

wines.name: Babo
wines.winemaking: Cool stainless steel. Immediate pressing, low-temperature ageing.
wines.convNote: Simple done well. This is Pinot Grigio from the northeastern corner of the Veneto -- closer to Alsace than to anything from a supermarket. Pear, white blossom, light citrus, clean finish. Good for guests who want something familiar but made with care.

wines.name: Chalmers Dott
wines.winemaking: Cool stainless steel. One of the rarest grapes in Australia.
wines.convNote: The Chalmers family run a specialist Italian variety nursery in Victoria and grow things no one else in Australia touches. Malvasia Istriana originates from the Istrian peninsula and is almost never seen outside of Friuli. Mandarin blossom, apricot, a waxy texture -- genuinely rare.

wines.name: Generazione Alessandro Trainara
wines.winemaking: Stainless steel. High on Etna's north-eastern slopes (around 650m) in volcanic sand. Terroir does the work.
wines.convNote: Mount Etna is having a moment and this is why. Grown high on Etna's north-eastern slopes in volcanic sand. Carricante and Catarratto produce something taut, mineral, and saline -- sometimes compared to Chablis but with a volcanic edge that's completely its own. One of the most interesting whites on the list.

wines.name: Pieropan Soave Classico
wines.winemaking: Brief skin maceration, old oak (texture not flavour), long lees ageing.
wines.convNote: The wine that makes people reconsider Soave. Pieropan has been farming the volcanic basalt hills above the town since 1880 and is widely considered the definitive producer. Garganega produces white peach, almond, lemon cream, and a slightly bitter citrus finish that's incredibly food-friendly. Ages beautifully.

wines.name: Charlotte Dalton Fred
wines.winemaking: Older oak fermentation with lees stirring (batonnage). Creamy texture, no oak flavour.
wines.convNote: Fiano is a grape from southern Italy -- warm, textural, nutty. In Langhorne Creek's warmth it becomes even richer, and the lees stirring adds a pillowy creaminess without losing freshness. White nectarine, honey, toasted nuts, lemon curd. Good for guests who find straight whites a bit austere.

wines.name: Stefanago Mischiabacche Bianco
wines.winemaking: Organic, no sulphur, no fining. Co-fermented in stainless steel.
wines.convNote: The name means 'mix of grapes' in local Lombard dialect -- Riesling, Muller-Thurgau, and Chardonnay from a certified organic estate. Lime zest, white flowers, stony mineral, flinty finish. Low intervention, high personality.

wines.name: Mortellito Viaria Bianco
wines.winemaking: Bone dry stainless steel. Extended lees contact for texture.
wines.producer: Il Mortellito -- a biodynamic estate near Noto, in south-east Sicily.
wines.convNote: Dry Moscato is a revelation. All the orange blossom and apricot aromatics you'd expect, but fermented bone-dry -- no sweetness, just structure and perfume. From a biodynamic estate near Noto, close to the Vendicari reserve and the sea at Marzamemi. For guests who think they don't like Moscato.

wines.name: Anne-Santi Ninfa del Nera
wines.winemaking: Organic stainless steel. Extended lees. Grechetto + Trebbiano.
wines.convNote: A tiny organic estate in the Valnerina limestone gorge in Umbria. Grechetto -- the backbone here -- has Greek origins and is one of Italy's most ancient grapes. White pear, hazelnut, meadow flowers, gentle spice, round texture. Gentle and food-friendly.

wines.name: Lamoresca Bianco
wines.winemaking: Biodynamic. Cement tanks -- no temperature control, no oak. Mineral texture.
wines.convNote: Biodynamic Vermentino from a tiny estate at 500 metres in central Sicily -- the opposite of the coastal, commercial style. Old bush vines in cement tanks. Crushed herbs, grapefruit, sea salt, fennel, bitter almond finish. Has real personality.

wines.name: Le Chiusure
wines.winemaking: Single vineyard. 12+ months on lees in stainless steel. Acidity needs time.
wines.convNote: One of Piedmont's best-kept secrets. Erbaluce means 'dawn grass' and grows near a glacier lake north of Turin. Extraordinary natural acidity, chalky mineral, green apple, white flowers, lime pith -- and it ages magnificently for ten years or more. A serious collector's wine at a reasonable price. Poured via Coravin -- a system that extracts wine through the cork using a fine needle and inert argon gas, so the bottle never has to be opened. This means we can offer this exceptional wine by the glass without the rest of the bottle oxidising, so you get to try something normally reserved for guests buying the full bottle.

wines.name: La Marca di San Michele Salta Tempo
wines.winemaking: 8 months in old oak foudres + lees stirring. Oak = texture, not flavour.
wines.convNote: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi is one of Italy's most underrated age-worthy whites. 'Salta Tempo' means skip time. Lemon cream, toasted almond, waxy texture from old oak, and that defining bitter almond finish. Made for food.

wines.name: Marabino Eureka
wines.winemaking: Partial barrel fermentation, 8 months French oak barriques + lees stirring.
wines.convNote: Biodynamic Chardonnay from a limestone plateau 400 metres above sea level in southeast Sicily. The elevation keeps it elegant -- yellow apple, vanilla cream, toasted brioche, round mouthfeel. Shows what Sicily can do with Chardonnay when the winemaker isn't trying to make a Burgundy imitation.

wines.name: Valli Unite Ciape
wines.winemaking: Workers' co-op. 12 months fine lees. No oak.
wines.convNote: A workers' cooperative founded in 1981 by three young farmers who chose the land over the city -- still collectively owned by its members. Cortese with more depth than most Gavi. Peach, almond, subtle floral, 12 months on fine lees. Honest and delicious.

wines.name: Tiberio
wines.winemaking: 12 months on lees. This Trebbiano rewards patience.
wines.convNote: This is the wine that proves Trebbiano d'Abruzzo is a serious grape. Most Trebbiano is watery bulk wine -- Tiberio's organically farmed version (uncertified by choice) from the hills between the Maiella and Gran Sasso is something else entirely. White peach, chamomile, mineral, lemon cream, long saline finish. Needs food.

wines.name: La Tosa Sorriso de Cielo
wines.winemaking: 12 hours skin contact, stainless steel, lees stirring. Aromatics do the work.
wines.convNote: 'Smile of the sky' -- dry aromatic Malvasia from an organic estate farming without chemicals for over 30 years. Orange blossom, mango, rose water, honey, a spiced finish. 12 hours of skin contact gives structure without going full orange wine.

wines.name: Meigamma Bianco Zero
wines.winemaking: Zero added sulphur. Indigenous yeasts, stainless steel.
wines.producer: Societa Agricola Meigamma -- Villasimius, on Sardinia's south-east coast.
wines.convNote: Zero added sulphur. Vermentino, Moscato and the ancient Nuragus grape, fermented on wild yeasts. The sandy vineyards sit barely 600 metres from the sea at Villasimius, and that maritime exposure shows -- bitter orange, wild herbs, a briny sea-salt lift, ancient earthiness. For guests who want something natural and genuinely unusual.

wines.name: Stropplatini
wines.winemaking: Stainless + old oak. 12+ months lees.
wines.producer: Stroppolatini -- an organic estate at Cividale del Friuli, in the Colli Orientali near the Slovenian border.
wines.convNote: Friulano's nutty, waxy, hay-like character is one of white wine's great flavour experiences. 12 months on lees in a mix of stainless and old oak. White almond, hay, bitter herbs, long finish. From ancient ponca soils near Slovenia.

wines.name: Vigneti Massa Derthona
wines.winemaking: 12+ months in large old oak. High extract + high acid + aromatics = needs time.
wines.convNote: Walter Massa single-handedly rescued Timorasso from extinction in the 1980s. 'Derthona' is the Latin name for Tortona. Quince, beeswax, white truffle, flint, extraordinary mineral depth. Can age 20 years. One of Italy's greatest whites.

wines.name: Fasoli Gino Oranghost
wines.winemaking: Weeks of skin contact: tannin, colour, texture. Disease-resistant, no spraying. Unfiltered.
wines.convNote: Orange wine gets its colour and tannin from weeks of skin contact. Souvignier Gris is a disease-resistant modern variety that needs no spraying. Bruised apple, dried apricot, earthy grip. Unfiltered, alive, a little wild. Gateway orange wine.

wines.name: Caruso and Minini Arancino
wines.winemaking: 7-10 days skin contact on Catarratto. Amber hue, white aromatics, red structure.
wines.convNote: Named for the Sicilian rice ball -- crispy outside, soft inside. Catarratto on skins for 7-10 days. Golden raisin, orange blossom, tannic grip, bitter marmalade. The easiest-drinking orange wine on the list -- good entry point for curious guests.

wines.name: Podere San Biagio Migrante
wines.winemaking: Extended skin maceration. Pecorino's high acidity balances the tannin from skins.
wines.producer: Fiore-Podere San Biagio -- Controguerra, in the Colline Teramane of northern Abruzzo, between the Adriatic and the Gran Sasso.
wines.convNote: Pecorino -- the 'sheep grape' -- given extended skin contact for an orange wine with grip. From Controguerra in the Teramo hills, where Adriatic breezes meet cool air spilling off the Gran Sasso. Tangerine, dried herbs, mountain mineral, savoury tannin. Serious and food-driven.

wines.name: Casa Brecceto Sassafrass Bianco
wines.winemaking: Extended skin maceration on ancient volcanic tuff soils. Smoky, chalky minerality.
wines.convNote: Greco di Tufo was brought to Campania by Greek colonists 2,500 years ago. Made as an orange wine on volcanic tuff soils -- amber tea, dried apricot, smoke, grippy volcanic finish. Ancient technique on an ancient grape.

wines.name: Etnella Attia Bianco
wines.winemaking: Pre-phylloxera own-rooted vines. Skin contact on volcanic ash. Chasselas adds Alpine note.
wines.convNote: Pre-phylloxera bush vines on Mount Etna -- own-rooted, never grafted, some over 100 years old. Pure black volcanic ash soils. Volcanic ash, dried flowers, wild herbs, extraordinary length. One of the most dramatic bottles on the list.

wines.name: Lunaria Ramoro
wines.winemaking: Ramoro: 24-48h skin maceration. Pinot Grigio's pink-grey skins give the copper colour.
wines.convNote: Ramoro means copper. Pinot Grigio's skins are naturally pinkish-grey; 24-48 hours of contact gives this its distinctive hue, light tannin, and red berry freshness. Organic, from Abruzzo. Predates modern pale rose by centuries.

wines.name: Giuseppe Cipolla Occhio di Sale
wines.winemaking: Nero d'Avola-led, with white varieties (Inzolia, Nerello Mascalese) co-fermented for lift. Spontaneous fermentation, brief skin contact, neutral vessels; organic farming. The salinity is drawn up from the salt- and gypsum-rich soils, not the sea.
wines.producer: Giuseppe Cipolla -- the Passofonduto project in the Platani River Valley near Agrigento, southern Sicily. A young natural grower (since around 2015) farming gypsum-rich hillsides that were once salt and sulfur mining country.
wines.convNote: 'Eye of salt' -- but the salt is in the ground, not the sea. Giuseppe Cipolla farms the gypsum- and halite-rich chalky soils of the Platani Valley near Agrigento, in Sicily's interior, where old salt and sulfur mines once worked. A Nero d'Avola-led blend with white grapes co-fermented: it drinks like a chilled light red -- wild strawberry, red cherry, citrus and florals, with a chalky, salty mineral crunch. Serve slightly chilled.

wines.name: Samodia Rosso
wines.winemaking: Still chilled red in the Emilian tradition. Serve 12-14 degrees C with charcuterie.
wines.producer: Samodia -- Jacopo Stigliano and Flavio Restani, in the Valsamoggia hills between Bologna and Modena.
wines.convNote: Emilia's chilled-red tradition, from the Apennine foothills of Valsamoggia -- whose ancient Latin name the project borrows -- at 400 to 500 metres between Bologna and Modena. Four varieties including Ancelotta and the Lambrusco grape Grasparossa. Dark cherry, plum, violet, earthy. Serve at 12-14 degrees with anything from the charcuterie section.

wines.name: Podere Guardia Grande Nascimento
wines.winemaking: 12 months large old oak. Cannonau = Grenache; more herbal and mineral in Sardinia.
wines.producer: Cantina Podere Guardia Grande -- a coastal estate above Capo Caccia near Alghero, in the Porto Conte reserve of north-west Sardinia.
wines.convNote: Sardinian Cannonau -- genetically Grenache, though Sardinians will argue it was theirs first. This grows on a wild coastal headland above Capo Caccia, inside the Porto Conte reserve near Alghero, where sea wind and maquis scrub leave their mark. Red cherry, dried herbs, leather, Mediterranean scrub, silky tannin. 12 months in large old oak.

wines.name: Gino Pedrotti
wines.winemaking: Short maceration preserves pale colour and low tannin. Serve slightly chilled.
wines.convNote: Schiava is the everyday red of the Alpine Tyrol -- light, pale, low tannin. Organic, from Lake Garda. Cranberry, rose hip, light smoke. Serve slightly chilled. Very easy drinking.

wines.name: Bio Vio U Bastio
wines.winemaking: Organic, hand-farmed vines near Albenga. Light extraction only. Rossese di Albenga -- grown just outside the neighbouring Dolceacqua DOC.
wines.producer: Bio Vio (Aimone Vio), Bastia d'Albenga, Liguria. An organic pioneer on the Riviera di Ponente and Gambero Rosso Winemaker of the Year 2017.
wines.convNote: Rossese from Aimone Vio, one of the first organic growers on Liguria's Riviera di Ponente. His U Bastio comes from Albenga, just outside the famous Dolceacqua zone, on lighter soils that give a more delicate, perfumed style. Red currant, violet, silky and fragrant with fine tannin. One of Italy's most charming light reds.

wines.name: L'Appel 'Ndom'
wines.winemaking: First crop from Teroldego vines planted by the Chalmers family at Heathcote in 2016. Hand harvested; 15% whole bunches under destemmed fruit, five days of cool pre-ferment maceration, then wild fermentation and natural malolactic in tank. Around 150 cases made.
wines.producer: L'Appel Wines, Victoria. A small-batch producer working with the Chalmers family's Heathcote vineyard -- the same Italian-variety specialists behind the Chalmers Dott on our white list.
wines.convNote: 'Ndom is northern Italian slang for 'let's go'. Teroldego is the deeply coloured alpine red of Trentino, and this is the first-ever crop from vines the Chalmers family planted at Heathcote in 2016 -- the same family behind the Chalmers Dott Malvasia. Blueberry, black cherry, cola and sweet anise over brambly earth, with the grape's naturally high acidity keeping it fresh and light on its feet. A genuine Australian rarity.

wines.name: Massimo Rivetti
wines.winemaking: Whole-cluster, 12 months French oak (30% new).
wines.convNote: Piedmont surprising the world with Pinot Nero. Whole-cluster fermentation and 12 months in French oak. Red cherry, earth, dried rose, forest floor, silky tannin. For guests who want Pinot Noir with a story beyond Burgundy.

wines.name: Occhipinti Fossa di Lupo
wines.winemaking: 70-year biodynamic bush vines. Cold maceration extracts aromatics not tannin. Old oak.
wines.convNote: Arianna Occhipinti started her estate at 21 and is now one of Italy's most celebrated natural winemakers. 'Wolf's Den' is her single-vineyard Frappatto from 70-year-old biodynamic vines. Pomegranate, wild strawberry, fresh herbs, extraordinary delicacy from hot Sicily. One of the great bottles on this list.

wines.name: Bera Barbera dAsti
wines.winemaking: Mix of stainless steel and old oak. Low tannin needs no new oak -- just time.
wines.convNote: Barbera is Piedmont's everyday grape -- high natural acidity, low tannin, maximum food compatibility. Black cherry, plum, tobacco, bright acidity, supple tannin. Works with almost everything on the menu.

wines.name: Custodi Pistus Etna Rosso
wines.winemaking: Old bush vines 600-900m on volcanic ash. Old oak. Mineral tension like fine Burgundy.
wines.convNote: Etna Rosso is the wine world's current obsession and this is a beautiful example of why. Old bush vines at 600-900 metres on volcanic ash -- Nerello Mascalese produces red cherry, blood orange, volcanic mineral, silky tannin. Sometimes compared to fine Burgundy but entirely its own thing.

wines.name: Musk Lane Wine 'Malakoff'
wines.winemaking: Nebbiolo from the Malakoff vineyard in the Victorian Pyrenees, planted from 1997 and widely credited as the vineyard that has done most for Australian Nebbiolo. Part of Musk Lane's single-vineyard 'Nebula' Nebbiolo series.
wines.producer: Musk Lane Wine, Kyneton, Victoria. An urban winery in a converted timber yard down a laneway in the Macedon Ranges town of Kyneton, open since 2019.
wines.convNote: Nebbiolo from the famous Malakoff vineyard in Victoria's Pyrenees -- arguably the single site that has done most to prove Nebbiolo belongs in Australia, supplying a who's who of Victorian winemakers. Musk Lane, an urban winery in Kyneton, bottles it as part of their Nebula series. Rose, orange peel and red cherry over a savoury, almost amaro-like herbal streak. For guests who love the Barbaresco but want to see what the grape does here.

wines.name: Arpepe Rosso di Valtellina
wines.winemaking: Chiavennasca (Nebbiolo) aged 24+ months old Slavonian oak. More delicate than Barolo.
wines.convNote: Steep granite terraces above the Adda river near Switzerland. Nebbiolo here is called Chiavennasca and produces something more delicate and alpine than the famous Langhe versions. Red cherry, rose, tar, mountain mineral, firm tannin. Needs time and food.

wines.name: Institut Agricole Regional
wines.winemaking: Cool alpine nights extend hang time. 8 months old oak. Darker and more mineral than Beaujolais.
wines.convNote: A winery that is also an agricultural school, training mountain farmers since 1951. Gamay in Valle d'Aosta loses the Beaujolais banana and gains mineral depth. Dark cherry, mountain violet, wild herbs, fresh acidity. Unusual and worth exploring. Poured via Coravin -- a system that extracts wine through the cork using a fine needle and inert argon gas, so the bottle never has to be opened. It lets us pour rare, premium bottles like this by the glass without the wine oxidising.

wines.name: Range Life Rosso
wines.winemaking: Separate ferments blended. 8 months older oak.
wines.convNote: Italian-inspired winemaking at honest prices from Victoria. Primitivo, Sangiovese, and Tempranillo together. Dark plum, blackberry, mocha, soft tannin. The wine for guests who want something generous and approachable without ceremony.

wines.name: Tenimenti Mancini 'Podere della Filandra' Chianti
wines.winemaking: Organic Chianti Colli Fiorentini. Sangiovese aged in large old oak.
wines.convNote: Organic Chianti from the Colli Fiorentini hills near Florence. Sangiovese aged in large old oak. Red cherry, leather, dried herbs, earthy, medium tannin. Classic with pasta and meat dishes.

wines.name: Produttori del Barbaresco
wines.winemaking: 26 months Slavonian oak (legal minimum). Needs 5-10+ years to open.
wines.convNote: Around fifty grower families in a cooperative since 1958, long celebrated as one of the world's great wine co-ops. Tar, roses, dried cherry, tobacco, formidable tannin. Needs 5-10 years to open but already incredible.

wines.name: Cantine Garrone Ca DMate Valli Ossolane Rosso
wines.winemaking: Prunent (the local name for Nebbiolo) in large old oak. Wilder and more tannic than Langhe.
wines.convNote: One of Italy's most remote wine regions -- steep mountain valleys near Switzerland, almost forgotten. Nebbiolo here (called Prunent) is wilder and more tannic than in the famous Langhe. Wild berry, tar, earth, mountain herbs, firm tannin. A discovery for Barolo lovers.

wines.name: Inkwell Road to Joy
wines.winemaking: Open-top, hand-plunged. 14 months older French oak. Organic.
wines.convNote: Organic McLaren Vale Shiraz with Primitivo -- Zinfandel's Italian twin. Open-top fermentation, hand-plunged, 14 months in older French oak. Dark chocolate, blackberry, mocha, vanilla, generous warm finish.

wines.name: Poggio Mandorlo Il Guardiano
wines.winemaking: 18 months French oak (50% new). Merlot smooth, Sangiovese acid.
wines.convNote: The Maremma was malarial swampland until the 1960s -- now some of Tuscany's most interesting wine country. Sangiovese and Merlot, 18 months in French oak. Black cherry, cedar, plum, tobacco, smooth tannin. Super Tuscan style at an approachable price.

wines.name: Alessandro di Camporeale Kaid
wines.winemaking: 14 months French oak. 400m prevents jammy overripeness.
wines.convNote: 'Kaid' is Arabic for leader -- Sicily was under Arab rule for 200 years. Syrah at 400 metres. Black olive, smoked meat, dark plum, white pepper, graphite. The altitude prevents the jammy overripeness you'd expect from Sicilian Syrah.

wines.name: Campo al Noce Miterre Bolgheri Rosso
wines.grape: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Syrah
wines.winemaking: Bordeaux method: 18 months French oak (40% new).
wines.convNote: Bolgheri is where Italian winemakers broke the law in the 1970s by planting Bordeaux varieties. This small independent estate continues that tradition. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cab Franc, Syrah -- blackcurrant, cedar, dark chocolate, bay leaf, firm structure.

wines.name: La Fornace Brunello di Montalcino Origini
wines.winemaking: Brunello's strict ageing: released only in the fifth year after harvest, with at least two years in oak. 100% Sangiovese.
wines.convNote: Italy's most prestigious wine. 100% Sangiovese, released only in its fifth year with a minimum of two years in oak. La Fornace farms the warmer southern slopes for a fuller style. Dried cherry, tar, earth, leather, extraordinary tannin. Can age 20-30 years. For the table celebrating something serious.

wines.name: Sa di Vino Gio
wines.winemaking: Stainless steel with extended lees contact. Viognier's natural richness preserved.
wines.producer: Emilia Romagna. Unusual Viognier from the Po Valley.
wines.convNote: Viognier in Emilia Romagna is an unusual find. Tropical fruit, peach blossom, honey, round and warm. For guests who like something with richness and fragrance but want to try something off the beaten track.

wines.name: San Lorenzo 'Di Gino Integrale'
wines.winemaking: Spontaneous fermentation in concrete vats, around nine months on the full fermentation lees in concrete, then bottled unfined and unfiltered with its own yeasts -- 'Integrale' means whole or unrefined. A magnum-only bottling of roughly 2,000 bottles. Certified organic and biodynamic farming.
wines.producer: Fattoria San Lorenzo, Montecarotto, Marche. Third-generation grower Natalino Crognaletti -- the estate is named for the hamlet of San Lorenzo, and this wine for his father Gino, a famed selector of Verdicchio clones.
wines.convNote: A magnum of benchmark natural Verdicchio from one of the Marche's great family estates. Natalino Crognaletti has near single-handedly proven Verdicchio can make complex, ageworthy whites. Bottled cloudy with its own lees -- expect pear, white flowers and a saline, sapid finish. May throw a little sediment, which is the point.

wines.name: Le Coste Litrozzo Rosato
wines.winemaking: Natural winemaking, minimal intervention. Serve chilled. A litre of pure pleasure.
wines.producer: Gradoli, Lazio. Le Coste is one of Italy's most celebrated natural wine estates.
wines.convNote: Le Coste is a legendary natural wine estate in volcanic Lazio. This litre of rosato -- Sangiovese, the rare Aleatico, and Procanico -- is made for a table that wants to drink something alive and delicious. Wild strawberry, herbs, saline finish. Serve cold.

wines.name: Sassara Vin da Cagnara Litro Rosso
wines.winemaking: Light maceration on Corvina. Serve chilled. A litre of the by-the-glass favourite.
wines.producer: Sassara Vini -- Valeggio sul Mincio, on the morainic hills just south-east of Lake Garda in Veneto.
wines.convNote: A litre of easygoing Corvina by the glass -- red cherry, violet, light and fresh. Grown on the glacial morainic hills above the Mincio, south-east of Lake Garda, on soils full of marine deposits, quartz and flint. The best format for a table that can't stop talking and keeps reaching for the bottle.

wines.name: Levi Serafino Arneis Vermouth
wines.winemaking: Arneis-based vermouth from Piedmont. Infused with botanicals, lightly sweet.
wines.producer: Distilleria Romano Levi, Neive, Piedmont. Founded 1925 by Serafino Levi. Romano Levi, known as 'the angelic grappa maker', is a legendary name in Piedmont. The vermouth recipe was discovered in the diaries of his sister Lidia, who grew botanicals in the distillery garden.
wines.convNote: Romano Levi was one of Piedmont's most beloved figures -- an eccentric grappa maker in Neive who drew his own bottle labels by hand and was known as the 'angelic grappa maker'. After his death, his family found recipe diaries kept by his sister Lidia, who had quietly cultivated herbs in the distillery garden for decades. This vermouth is made from those recipes -- Arneis base, Langhe herbs, elderberry, orange, artemisia, with a touch of their own grappa to finish. A genuinely rare piece of Piedmontese history.

wines.name: Cocchi Americano Vermouth
wines.winemaking: Moscato d'Asti base infused with gentian, cinchona bark, and citrus. The classic Cocchi house style -- lighter and more floral than a red vermouth.
wines.producer: Cocchi, Asti, Piedmont. Founded 1891. One of the great historic vermouth houses of Piedmont.
wines.convNote: Cocchi Americano is what you'd pour if James Bond had better taste. Moscato d'Asti base with gentian and quinine -- pale, floral, and bracingly refreshing. The classic Vesper ingredient.

wines.name: Saison White Flowers Vermouth
wines.winemaking: Melbourne-made vermouth on a Muscat base. Botanical infusion focused on white flowers and citrus -- lighter and more aromatic than Italian styles.
wines.producer: Saison Aperitifs, Melbourne. Founded 2020 by Dave Verheul, chef-owner of Embla and Lesa in Melbourne's CBD.
wines.convNote: Dave Verheul is one of Melbourne's most celebrated chefs -- co-owner of Embla on Flinders Lane, where natural wine and wood-fired cooking meet. In 2020, during the pandemic, he turned a house vermouth project into Saison Aperitifs, making small-batch vermouths using peak-season botanicals sourced from biodynamic farms. The first release sold out in a week. White Flowers is his lightest expression -- jasmine, elderflower, lemon zest. Half as sweet as a European vermouth, meant to be drunk over ice. A genuinely Melbourne story.

wines.name: Aetnae Etna Aperitif
wines.winemaking: Made on a Nerello Mascalese base from Mount Etna. Botanical infusion inspired by the herbs and citrus growing on the volcano's slopes.
wines.producer: Aetnae, Mount Etna, Sicily. A volcanic aperitif project using Nerello Mascalese from Etna's slopes.
wines.convNote: An aperitif made from Nerello Mascalese grown on Mount Etna -- blood orange, bitter herbs, a volcanic mineral smokiness. Unique in the world. Great for guests who've loved the Etna wines.

wines.name: Cappelano Barolo Chinato
wines.winemaking: Barolo (Nebbiolo) infused with china bark (quinine), rhubarb, cardamom, and other botanicals. Served with soda and lemon. One of Italy's oldest digestivo traditions.
wines.producer: Cappelano, Serralunga d'Alba, Piedmont. One of Barolo's most traditional estates, making Chinato the old-fashioned way since the 19th century.
wines.convNote: Barolo Chinato is one of Italy's great digestivo traditions -- real Barolo wine infused with quinine bark, rhubarb, and spice. Cappelano is the benchmark. Serve with soda and lemon. Extraordinary.

wines.name: Podere Pradarolo Frinire di Cicale
wines.winemaking: 500ml. Malvasia di Candia Aromatica harvested late for natural sweetness. Zero sulphur. One of Emilia Romagna's most distinctive dessert wines.
wines.producer: Podere Pradarolo, Varano de Melegari, Emilia Romagna. A leading natural wine estate making zero-sulphur wines from indigenous varieties.
wines.convNote: Frinire di Cicale -- 'cricket's chirp' -- is a 500ml dessert wine from Emilia Romagna. Malvasia di Candia Aromatica at its most expressive: apricot, orange blossom, honey. Zero sulphur, completely natural. Stunning with cheese or just on its own.

wines.name: Maria al Monte Limoncello
wines.winemaking: Ligurian limoncello made with hand-harvested Sfusato lemons from the coastal cliffs. Cold infusion preserves the essential oils in the peel.
wines.producer: Maria al Monte, Liguria. Hand-harvested Sfusato lemons from coastal cliff terraces above the Ligurian sea.
wines.convNote: Limoncello from Liguria -- the Italian Riviera coast where lemon groves cling to cliff terraces. Fresh lemon zest, sweet and bright. The real thing, not the tourist version.

wines.name: Nonino Vendemmia Grappa
wines.winemaking: Vendemmia means harvest -- this is a single-harvest grappa made from fresh grape pomace immediately after picking. Lighter and more aromatic than aged grappa.
wines.producer: Distilleria Nonino, Percoto, Friuli. The family that transformed grappa from rough firewater into a fine spirit, inventing the single-variety style in 1973.
wines.convNote: The Nonino family invented single-variety grappa in the 1970s and transformed it from rough firewater into something worth drinking slowly. Vendemmia is their fresh-harvest style -- floral, clean, light. The entry point to fine grappa.

wines.name: La Chiuse Grappa Riserva
wines.winemaking: Riserva means aged in oak -- this Sangiovese pomace grappa has been matured in small barrels, picking up vanilla, spice, and a golden colour. Softer and more complex than unaged grappa.
wines.producer: La Chiuse, Montalcino, Tuscany. A Brunello di Montalcino estate -- the Sangiovese pomace used for this grappa comes from their Brunello vineyards.
wines.convNote: Grappa from the Brunello di Montalcino estate La Chiuse -- the pomace is the leftover Sangiovese skins from making Brunello. Aged in oak barrels: vanilla, dried fruit, tobacco. A serious digestivo.

wines.name: Cocchi Vermouth di Torino
wines.winemaking: The classic sweet red vermouth style -- Moscato d'Asti base with a secret botanical recipe unchanged since 1891. The template for the Negroni and countless classic cocktails.
wines.producer: Cocchi, Turin, Piedmont. Founded 1891. The historic recipe that defined the sweet red Turin vermouth style.
wines.convNote: The vermouth that helped invent the Negroni. Cocchi di Torino is a sweet red vermouth with cocoa, orange peel, and bitter herbs -- a historic recipe from 1891. Drink it on ice, in a Negroni, or with soda.

wines.name: Furlani Amaro
wines.convNote: A rare artisan amaro from Trentino, made by a small family distillery in the Dolomites. Alpine herbs, gentian, and mountain roots give it a clean, bracing bitterness. Less well-known than its famous neighbours but genuinely excellent.

wines.name: Cappelletti Amaro Pasubio
wines.convNote: Named for Mount Pasubio, scene of brutal WWI fighting in the Trentino Alps. Cappelletti has been making bitter liqueurs since 1896. This is their alpine amaro -- bitter, herbal, and historically rooted.

wines.name: Amaro Alpino
wines.convNote: A classic alpine amaro from Trentino. Made with a blend of mountain herbs including gentian, wormwood, and alpine flowers. The Dolomites in a glass -- clean, bitter, and refreshing over ice.

wines.name: Cappelletti Amaro Sfumato Rabarbo
wines.convNote: 'Sfumato' means smoky and 'rabarbo' is rhubarb -- and both are immediately apparent. A distinctive, slightly smoky rhubarb-driven amaro from the Cappelletti family. One of the more unusual flavours on the list.

wines.name: Amaro Nonino
wines.convNote: The Nonino family invented single-variety grappa and transformed Italian distilling. Their amaro -- built on a grappa base with mountain herbs -- is one of Italy's most balanced and elegant. Lighter and more refined than most.

wines.name: Liquore delle Sirene Canto Amaro
wines.convNote: 'Song of the Sirens' -- a small-production Lombard amaro with Mediterranean citrus and alpine herb character. Named for the mythological sirens of the Italian coastline. Aromatic and complex.

wines.name: Braulio
wines.convNote: Made in Bormio in the Lombard Alps since 1875, aged in oak barrels in mountain cellars. One of Italy's great traditional amaros -- juniper, wormwood, yarrow, and Alpine herbs. The standard digestivo of the Valtellina mountain communities.

wines.name: Fernet Branca
wines.convNote: The world's most famous amaro, made in Milan since 1845 to a 27-herb secret recipe. Intensely bitter, minty, and medicinal. Either you love it or you don't -- but every bartender in the world knows it. The digestivo of digestivos.

wines.name: La Valdotaine Amaro Dente di Leone
wines.convNote: 'Dente di Leone' is dandelion -- the primary botanical in this amaro from Italy's smallest and most mountainous region. La Valdotaine distillery sits at the foot of Mont Blanc. Herbal, earthy, and distinctly alpine.

wines.name: Amaro Rubino
wines.convNote: A Piedmontese amaro with a wine-forward base and ruby red colour -- hence the name. Made with Barolo grape pomace and local herbs. More wine-like and approachable than most amaros.

wines.name: Bordiga Chiot Montamaro
wines.convNote: Bordiga has been distilling in Cuneo, at the foot of the Maritime Alps, since 1888. Chiot Montamaro is their alpine amaro -- gentian, gentian, and mountain herbs with a clean bitter finish. Great value.

wines.name: Amarot 8
wines.convNote: A modern Piedmontese amaro made with eight botanicals -- the name says it all. Clean, balanced, and less challenging than some on this list. Good entry point for guests new to amaro.

wines.name: Cardamaro Vermouth Amaro
wines.convNote: A hybrid sitting between vermouth and amaro -- wine-based, flavoured with cardoon (wild artichoke) and blessed thistle. Lower alcohol than most amaros, more approachable, and excellent on ice with soda. Made by the Bosca family in Piedmont.

wines.name: Marolo Ulrich Amaro
wines.convNote: Distilleria Marolo in Alba makes some of Piedmont's finest grappas and liqueurs. Their Ulrich amaro uses local Langhe herbs and a grappa base -- bitter, spiced, and deeply rooted in the landscape around Barolo and Barbaresco.

wines.name: Gualco Amaro Soldatini
wines.convNote: 'Soldatini' means little soldiers -- a reference to the small botanical soldiers fighting in every sip. Distilleria Gualco is a family operation in Piedmont making small-batch spirits. Rare, well-made, and worth the premium.

wines.name: Antico Amaro Noveis
wines.convNote: From Distillerie Francoli in Ghemme, Piedmont. 'Noveis' references Novese -- the local area. An old-style Piedmontese amaro with gentian, citrus peel, and warming spice. Traditional and well-balanced.

wines.name: Antico Fernet Noveis
wines.convNote: The Fernet-style sibling from Distillerie Francoli -- more minty and medicinal than the Amaro Noveis. Fernet style means intensely bitter and herbal, with a strong menthol note. For the committed amaro drinker.

wines.name: Amaro Montenegro
wines.convNote: Named for Princess Elena of Montenegro who married the Italian king in 1896. One of Italy's most beloved amaros -- made in Bologna with 40 botanicals including sweet orange, vanilla, and eucalyptus. Sweeter and more approachable than most. The gateway amaro.

wines.name: Dibaldo Un Bitter
wines.convNote: From the same Dibaldo distillery behind the Nostradamus gin on the cocktail list. Un Bitter is their Campari-style bitter aperitivo -- bright red, citrus-forward, and significantly more complex than the industrial alternative. A genuine small-batch version of a classic format.

wines.name: Ca de Noci La Rugiada di San Giovanni
wines.convNote: *Contains nuts. 'La Rugiada di San Giovanni' -- the Dew of Saint John, referring to the midsummer night when herbs are said to be at their most potent. Ca de Noci is a walnut and wine estate in Emilia Romagna. This nocino-style liqueur is made with green walnuts harvested at midsummer. Extraordinary.

wines.name: Meletti Amaro
wines.convNote: Made in Ascoli Piceno in the Marche since 1870. One of Italy's oldest and most consistently excellent amaros -- saffron, anise, and alpine herbs in a dark, rich base. The saffron note is distinctive and immediately recognisable.

wines.name: Casamari Elixir di San Bernardo
wines.convNote: Made by Cistercian monks at the Casamari Abbey in Lazio, founded in 1203. The monks have been producing this herbal elixir for centuries using a recipe of over 30 herbs grown in the abbey garden. One of the few genuinely monastic Italian amaros still in production.

wines.name: Cynar
wines.convNote: The artichoke amaro. Cynar is made primarily from artichoke leaves -- the name comes from 'Cynara', the botanical name for artichoke. Bittersweet, earthy, and surprisingly versatile. Famous for being served over ice with soda and orange in northern Italy.

wines.name: Rucolino
wines.convNote: A hyper-local Neapolitan liqueur made from wild rocket (rucola) grown on the island of Ischia in the Bay of Naples. Unique in the world -- peppery, herbal, with a distinctive green character. Almost impossible to find outside of Ischia and the best Italian restaurants.

wines.name: Cafo Vecchio Amaro del Capo
wines.convNote: From the toe of the Italian boot -- Calabria, home of bergamot and some of Italy's most intense citrus. Amaro del Capo is made with 29 herbs and spices and is traditionally served ice-cold, straight from the freezer. One of Italy's most popular digestivos.

wines.name: Cartamaro
wines.convNote: A contemporary Sardinian amaro using native island botanicals -- myrtle, cistus, and Mediterranean herbs found only on the island. Made by the same producer as Bomba Carta. Distinctly Sardinian in character.

wines.name: Bomba Carta
wines.convNote: 'Bomba Carta' is a traditional Sardinian paper firecracker used at festivals. This amaro -- made with native Sardinian botanicals -- has the same explosive energy. Bitter, aromatic, and deeply tied to the island's culture.

wines.name: Bresca Dorada Mirto
wines.convNote: Mirto is Sardinia's national liqueur -- made from the berries of the myrtle bush that covers the island's hillsides. Bresca Dorada (golden honeycomb) is one of the finest producers. Dark purple, richly aromatic, sweet-bitter. Served ice-cold after dinner.

wines.name: Citrange Limone
wines.convNote: A Sicilian citrus liqueur-amaro hybrid using the citrange -- a cross between citrus and trifoliate orange that grows on the slopes of Mount Etna. Bright, bitter, and intensely citrus-forward. A taste of volcanic Sicily.

wines.name: Amaro Nepeta
wines.convNote: Nepeta is wild catnip -- an aromatic herb native to Sicily used in traditional medicine for centuries. This amaro from southeast Sicily is built around it. Herbaceous, slightly minty, and deeply aromatic. A Sicilian amaro that tastes completely unlike anything from the north.

wines.name: Amaro Averna
wines.convNote: One of Italy's most famous amaros, made in Caltanissetta, Sicily since 1868. The original recipe was given to Salvatore Averna by Benedictine monks of the Santo Spirito Abbey. Rich, bittersweet, with notes of citrus, liquorice, and caramel. The quintessential Sicilian digestivo.

wines.name: Saison Artichoke Vin Amaro
wines.convNote: Dave Verheul's wine-based amaro -- lower alcohol, built on a Victorian wine base with artichoke and seasonal botanicals. A lighter, more food-friendly style than traditional Italian amaro. The Australian answer to Cynar.

wines.name: Saison Blackcurrant Leaf Vin Amaro
wines.convNote: Dave Verheul's blackcurrant leaf amaro -- made with leaves from Victorian blackcurrant bushes, not the fruit. The leaf has a distinctive green, tannic, almost smoky character quite unlike blackcurrant juice. Unique and very Melbourne.

wines.name: Starward Regal Rogue Bold Aged Amaro
wines.convNote: A collaboration between Melbourne whisky distillery Starward and Regal Rogue vermouth. Aged in Starward's Australian whisky barrels -- the oak and whisky character gives this amaro a distinctive warmth and vanilla note found nowhere else.

wines.name: Autonomy Native Australian Amaro
wines.convNote: Made entirely with native Australian botanicals -- lemon myrtle, wattle seed, mountain pepper, and others. A genuinely Australian take on the Italian tradition. For guests who want something that couldn't exist anywhere else.

wines.name: Sweetdram Whisky Amaro
wines.convNote: A Scottish whisky amaro from Edinburgh -- Scotch whisky base infused with Italian amaro botanicals. The meeting point of two bitter traditions. Smoky, herbal, and completely its own thing. For guests who like whisky and want something unusual.

wines.name: Stellacino Amaro London
wines.convNote: A London-made amaro inspired by the Italian tradition but using British botanicals alongside classical Italian herbs. Named for the Italian practice of drinking amaro under the stars ('stelle'). The international reach of the amaro movement in one bottle.

wines.name: Fernet-Gambarotta Menta 1963
wines.convNote: A 1963 vintage Fernet from Gambarotta -- a now-defunct Lombard producer. Over 60 years in the bottle has transformed it completely: the mint has softened into something more complex and almost savoury. A genuine piece of Italian drinking history. Served in 30ml pours.

wines.name: Casauria Antico Amaro Abruzzese 1983
wines.convNote: A 1983 vintage amaro from the Casauria estate in Abruzzo -- now over 40 years old. The Abruzzese herbal tradition meets decades of slow oxidation in glass. Something you simply cannot find anywhere else. Served in 30ml pours.

wines.name: Tilus Amaro al Tartufo 1978
wines.convNote: A 1978 truffle amaro from the tiny republic of San Marino -- one of the world's smallest countries, entirely surrounded by Italy. Truffle-infused amaro from 1978 is an extraordinary thing: earthy, fungal, and unlike anything else on any list anywhere. Served in 30ml pours.

wines.name: Valli Unite Rosatea
wines.winemaking: Co-fermented field blend of red and white grapes from the Valli Unite cooperative.
wines.producer: Colli Tortonesi, Piedmont. Workers cooperative since 1981.
wines.convNote: From the same workers cooperative that makes the Ciape white. Rosatea co-ferments Cortese (white) with Barbera, Freisa, and Malvasia. Wild strawberry, cherry, floral lift, earthy undertone. Chillable and food-friendly.

wines.name: Blood Moon Promise
wines.winemaking: Schioppettino on ancient Cambrian soils in Heathcote. One of very few plantings of this rare Friulian variety in Australia.
wines.producer: Blood Moon, Heathcote, Victoria. Small producer on 500-million-year-old Cambrian soils.
wines.convNote: Blood Moon is a small Heathcote producer working with rare Italian varieties. Their Schioppettino -- the little explosion grape -- is one of only a handful of plantings outside Friuli, on Heathcote's ancient 500-million-year-old Cambrian soils. Black pepper, wild berry, violet. Distinctive and worth seeking out.

wines.name: Carousal
wines.winemaking: Whole berries into a large open fermenter, one gentle pump-over a day for a slow four-week ferment, then pressed to old barriques for a short rest before bottling. Fruit from the Walpole family's Bungamero vineyard at Whorouly South, planted to superior Mat 6 and Mat 7 Sangiovese clones.
wines.producer: Carousal, Alpine Valleys, Victoria. A side project from Patrick Sullivan and his wife Megan, exploring Italian varieties beyond their Gippsland home base.
wines.convNote: Same winemaker as our Continental Platter Prosecco -- Patrick Sullivan, one of Victoria's most respected natural winemakers. Carousal means a wild, joyful party, and the wine matches: bright cherry and raspberry Sangiovese from the Alpine Valleys with lively acidity and classic dusty tannins. Honest farming, serious drinkability.

wines.name: Caruso and Minini Frappello
wines.winemaking: Blend of Frappato and Nerello Mascalese from western Sicily. Light extraction, early bottling.
wines.producer: Caruso and Minini, western Sicily near Marsala. Same estate as the Arancino orange wine.
wines.convNote: From the same Caruso and Minini estate as the Arancino orange wine. Frappello blends Frappato (the delicate grape of Vittoria) with Nerello Mascalese (the great red of Etna). Pomegranate, wild strawberry, violet, light tannin. Two of Sicily's finest red varieties together in one elegant glass.

wines.name: Leeona Rosso
wines.winemaking: Co-fermented with white Malvasia Bianca. Ancient Tuscan practice for perfume and lightness.
wines.producer: Tuscany. Historical practice: white grapes co-fermented with red.
wines.convNote: An ancient Tuscan practice: adding white Malvasia Bianca to red Sangiovese during fermentation adds perfume and lightens the body in a way you can't achieve by blending after the fact. Cherry, violet, white pepper, floral lift. More nuanced than a straight Chianti.

wines.name: Fangareggi Biancospino
wines.winemaking: Traditional Lambrusco method -- refermented in tank to produce a light frizzante sparkle. Lambrusco di Sorbara is considered the finest of the Lambrusco varieties.
wines.producer: Fangareggi, Emilia Romagna. Specialist in the rare Lambrusco di Sorbara variety.
wines.convNote: Lambrusco di Sorbara is considered the finest and most delicate of all the Lambrusco varieties -- grown only in a small area near Modena. Biancospino (hawthorn) is a pale, delicate sparkling red with wild strawberry, violet, and floral notes. A revelation for anyone who thinks Lambrusco is the sweet red from the 1980s.

wines.name: Longarico All Ombra dei Pini
wines.winemaking: Traditional method sparkling wine from Catarratto -- an unusual choice for the format. Aged on lees in bottle for complexity.
wines.producer: Longarico -- Catarratto grown on Monte Bonifato, near Alcamo in western Sicily. 'All'Ombra dei Pini' means in the shade of the pines.
wines.convNote: A traditional-method Sicilian sparkling from Catarratto, the classic white grape of the island's west. Grown on the slopes of Monte Bonifato above Alcamo -- limestone, not lava -- where altitude keeps it taut. Toasty bottle-age complexity meets a saline, citrus-driven core. Lemon zest, white flowers, long mineral finish.

wines.name: Biscaris
wines.winemaking: Stainless steel. Inzolia harvested early to preserve acidity and freshness.
wines.producer: Biscaris -- Inzolia from Acate, in south-east Sicily's Vittoria country.
wines.convNote: Inzolia is an ancient Sicilian grape that once formed the backbone of Marsala. Today progressive growers vinify it bone-dry to show its almond-and-citrus side. This comes from Acate, inland in the south-east near Vittoria -- dry, fresh and mineral, with far more nerve than Inzolia's old reputation suggests.

wines.name: Niklas Weingut
wines.winemaking: Stainless steel fermentation. Pinot Bianco in Alto Adige is picked early to preserve acid tension. No malolactic fermentation.
wines.producer: Niklas Weingut, Sudtirol-Alto Adige. Alpine estate in the bilingual Italian-German south.
wines.convNote: Alto Adige's Pinot Bianco (Weissburgunder in German) is considered among the finest expressions of the variety in the world. At Niklas, the alpine climate -- warm days, very cold nights -- concentrates flavour while retaining vivid acidity. The region changed hands from Austria to Italy after WWI and remains bilingual today.

wines.name: Il Modo Bianco
wines.winemaking: Minimal intervention. No fining or filtration. Vermentino, Fiano and Riesling co-fermented in stainless steel.
wines.producer: Il Modo, Geelong, Victoria. Italian varieties in volcanic Geelong soils.
wines.convNote: Il Modo (the way) reflects the winemaker's philosophy of minimal intervention. A blend of Vermentino, Fiano, and Riesling grown in volcanic Geelong soils -- three Italian-origin varieties that together produce something broader and more complex than any one alone. No fining, no filtration.

wines.name: Crotin Aris
wines.winemaking: Freisa d'Asti in its dry, serious form. Aged in old oak. Freisa is Nebbiolo's close cousin.
wines.producer: Crotin, Asti, Piedmont. Freisa specialist in the Monferrato hills.
wines.convNote: Freisa is Nebbiolo's little-known cousin -- grown in the same hills but rarely seen outside Piedmont. Crotin's Aris is the dry, serious version: red cherry, violet, earthy tannin, fresh acidity. A genuinely rare Piedmontese variety that rewards the curious table.

wines.name: Cretapaglia Folk
wines.winemaking: Pecorello -- a rare Calabrian grape -- made as an orange wine with extended skin contact. Natural winemaking, minimal intervention.
wines.producer: Cretapaglia, Calabria. Specialist in the rare Pecorello variety.
wines.convNote: Pecorello is a near-forgotten Calabrian grape revived by a handful of natural winemakers. Cretapaglia's Folk gives it extended skin contact -- dried apricot, wild herbs, savoury tannin grip. One of the rarest grapes on the entire list, from Italy's toe.

wines.name: Momento Mori Etcetera Etcetera
wines.winemaking: A chillable blend of the rare Schioppettino with Syrah -- light extraction for an easy-drinking, food-friendly red.
wines.producer: Momento Mori, Heathcote, Victoria. Natural wine producer working with rare varieties.
wines.convNote: Momento Mori blends the rare Schioppettino with Syrah for a chillable, easy-drinking red. Red cherry, black pepper, violet, light tannin. 'Etcetera Etcetera' is exactly the kind of playful naming this Heathcote producer is known for. Serve slightly chilled.

wines.name: Wilfred Monte
wines.winemaking: Montepulciano grown in warm McLaren Vale -- an unusual variety choice for the region. Minimal intervention winemaking.
wines.convNote: Montepulciano is usually associated with Abruzzo, but Wilfred Monte proves it thrives in warm McLaren Vale too. Dark plum, dried herbs, earthy tannin, warm spice. An unusual and excellent Australian take on an Italian variety not normally seen outside its homeland.

wines.name: Fattoria di Bacchereto 'Terre a Mano'
wines.winemaking: Carmignano DOCG -- biodynamically farmed since 2002. Hand-harvested, fermented with indigenous yeasts, aged around 26 months in Allier oak tonneaux on fine lees, unfined and unfiltered.
wines.producer: Fattoria di Bacchereto, Carmignano, Tuscany. Run by Rossella Bencini Tesi -- one of only 14 producers in Italy's smallest, and among its oldest, appellations.
wines.convNote: Carmignano is a tiny, historic corner of Tuscany near Florence with an unusual rule: Sangiovese must share the blend with a splash of Cabernet Sauvignon, a tradition dating back to Catherine de Medici. This biodynamic bottling from Fattoria di Bacchereto is unfined, unfiltered, and spends close to two years in oak -- structured, earthy, and built for the table.

wines.name: I Love Monsters 'La Birba' Pet Nat
wines.winemaking: Ancestral-method pet nat (petillant naturel) from 100% Lacrima di Morro d'Alba. A brief skin maceration gives the salmon-pink colour; refermented in bottle with no added yeast or sugar, unfiltered, sur lie under a crown cap. Certified organic.
wines.producer: I Love Monsters -- the playful natural-wine offshoot of Tenuta di Tavignano in Le Marche, run by second-generation owner Ondine.
wines.convNote: A crown-capped, cloudy pet nat that drinks like summer in a bottle. Made from Lacrima -- Marche's perfumed local red -- given just enough skin contact to blush salmon-pink. Strawberry and white flowers with a doughy, yeasty edge from the lees. Bone-dry, bouncy and refreshing; brilliant with vegetables, snacks or anything spiced.

wines.name: Stelios Kimonides
wines.winemaking: Skin-contact (orange) Moscato Bianco -- the aromatic grape macerated on its skins to draw out texture and a pale-copper hue. Minimal-intervention natural winemaking; dry despite the perfumed nose.
wines.producer: Steve (Stelios) Kimonides -- a Melbourne winemaker and skin-contact specialist, also the wine buyer at Rumi.
wines.convNote: Moscato you can drink with dinner. Steve Kimonides macerates the aromatic grape on its skins, turning all that heady perfume -- orange blossom, jasmine, Turkish delight -- into a dry, pale-copper orange wine with a gentle phenolic grip. Riverland fruit, natural hands.

wines.name: Maidenii Yuzu Vermouth
wines.winemaking: An extra-dry vermouth built on an amphora-fermented Greco base from Heathcote. Botanicals lead with yuzu and native Australian citrus, backed by wormwood, salmon gum and chestnut flowers.
wines.producer: Maidenii -- the celebrated collaboration between French winemaker Gilles Lapalus and Australian bartender Shaun Byrne, showcasing native Victorian botanicals.
wines.convNote: Australia's most inventive vermouth house turns to yuzu. Extra-dry, built on amphora-fermented Heathcote Greco, with yuzu and native citrus lifting a wormwood-and-salmon-gum backbone. Serve over ice, lengthen with soda, or stir into a razor-sharp martini.

cocktails.name: Pasubio Manhattan
cocktails.ingredients: Woodford Reserve Bourbon, Cappelletti Pasubio Amaro, Orange Bitters
cocktails.story: A Manhattan riff using Cappelletti Pasubio amaro from Trentino instead of sweet vermouth. The mountain herbs give it a distinctive bitter complexity alongside the Woodford's caramel warmth.

cocktails.name: Bello Cello
cocktails.ingredients: Tequila Blanco, Limoncello, Cucumber, Lime, Chilli
cocktails.story: The limoncello from the digestivo list makes an appearance here -- adding a sweet Italian citrus note to the tequila base. Bright, fresh, and a little spicy.

cocktails.name: Negroni Mora
cocktails.ingredients: Beefeater Gin, Plymouth Sloe Gin, Campari, Blackberry
tastingNotes: Bitter-sweet balance -- juniper and berry richness with a dry finish
Classic Negroni structure with blackberry depth from sloe gin
Stirred and spirit-forward -- complex bitter orange and red berry
Bold and aromatic -- for guests who enjoy bitter, herbal cocktails
Rich berry sweetness balanced by Campari bitterness and gin botanicals

cocktails.name: Fig Spritz
cocktails.ingredients: Pot and Still Fig Liqueur, Prosecco, Soda, Lemon
tastingNotes: Light and low-ABV -- fig sweetness lifted by Prosecco bubbles and lemon
Easy-drinking and aromatic -- perfect aperitivo style
Fruity and effervescent -- sweeter than an Aperol spritz with fig depth
Refreshing and sessionable -- great for guests who want something light
Fine bubbles with sweet fig and bright citrus finish

cocktails.name: Tommy Dibaldo Sour
cocktails.ingredients: Dibaldo Nostradamus Gin, Tommy's Kiwi, Lemon
tastingNotes: Bright and tropical -- botanical gin with kiwi fruit and fresh lemon
Citrus-forward sour with a foamy texture and unexpected kiwi sweetness
Tart and refreshing -- gin-based with a New Zealand fruit twist
Lively and aromatic -- for guests who enjoy sours with a fruit character
Balanced sweet-sour with gin botanicals and tropical kiwi notes

cocktails.name: Martini Your Way
cocktails.ingredients: Gin -- served dry, dirty, or gibson style
tastingNotes: Clean and concentrated -- bone dry gin with aromatic vermouth and citrus
Spirit-forward and elegant -- for guests who want something classic
Dry and precise -- juniper-led with a saline or briny finish depending on style
The driest cocktail on the menu -- all about the quality of the gin
Stirred to order -- three styles: dry, dirty with brine, or Gibson with onion
